column1: It's not just oil and natural gas production that's booming; we're becoming a global leader in clean energy. More and more people are seeing the benefits of solar and wind. Businesses are investing in energy efficiency. And because of these advances, along with the President’s initiatives, we are creating jobs and growing an economy for the future. Americans can adapt, they meet challenges, and we can out-innovate any other country if we set our minds to it. We've never been a nation to shy away from a challenge and we can't go back.

Now, little more than 40 years ago, astronauts descended the nine-rung ladder of the lunar module and walked on the moon. This extraordinary feat of human endeavor has long inspired generations. It remains a source of pride and wonder for all Americans, and a reminder of what we can achieve when we work together, pushing the boundaries of what is possible. Because whenever we’ve been willing to dream big, to invest in science and technology, to take risks and explore, to explore our world and beyond, we’ve discovered new frontiers.

We agree that real opportunity requires every American to get the education and training they deserve. This is why we're working with states to make college more affordable, and help more Americans to graduate without a mountain of debt. Because if you can't afford to go to college, or saddled with debt when you do, then you're not as free to pursue your dreams. We also know that opportunity requires a level playing field.

For we, the people, understand that our country cannot succeed when a shrinking few do well while more and more of those who are working and paying taxes find themselves struggling to get by. That's why, over the past seven years, we've worked every single day to build an economy that works for everybody. An economy that rewards hard work and responsibility, not just wealth. An economy where everyone gets a fair shot, and everyone does their fair share.

One senator, as you all are aware, had put a hold on every single nominee for the Department of Justice. The purpose? To prevent a vote on the legislation that would have made it easier for women to get equal pay for equal work. And as I said, this isn't about party politics. This is about common sense. It's about making sure that, in America, everyone gets a fair shot -- this is about making sure that hard work is rewarded, and that every single person has an opportunity to make it to the top of the economic ladder.
